question.questionText: We worked hard just before Christmas ________  we could really enjoy the holiday.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
In this sentence, we need to express the purpose of working hard before Christmas. The correct structure to show purpose is 'so that + subject + can/could + verb'. 'So that' is used to indicate the reason or purpose for an action, especially when the subject of the two clauses is different or when we want to specify the result. The sentence is: 'We worked hard just before Christmas so that we could really enjoy the holiday.'
  • to (preposition): 'To' is used to express purpose, but it is followed directly by a verb (to + V-infinitive) and is used when the subject of both actions is the same. In this sentence, it could be used, but 'so that' is more appropriate because it allows for a subject and modal verb in the second clause.
  • in order to (phrase): 'In order to' is also used to express purpose and is followed by a verb (in order to + V-infinitive). Like 'to', it is used when the subject of both actions is the same. Here, 'so that' is better because it introduces a new subject and modal verb.
  • so that (conjunction): 'So that' is a conjunction used to express purpose, especially when the second clause has a different subject or uses a modal verb (can/could/will/would). It fits perfectly in this sentence.
Related structure or vocabulary: so that + subject + can/could/will/would + verb: used to express purpose or result

question.questionText: John just popped out _________ the paper.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank in the sentence 'John just popped out _________ the paper.' requires an infinitive verb form to express the purpose of the action. In English, the structure 'pop out to do something' is commonly used to indicate that someone leaves briefly in order to do a specific action.
  • for buy (preposition + verb (incorrect form)): 'for' is a preposition and must be followed by a noun or gerund (V-ing), not the base form of a verb. 'for buy' is grammatically incorrect.
  • buy (verb (base form)): Using the base form 'buy' alone after 'popped out' is incorrect. The sentence needs an infinitive ('to buy') to indicate purpose.
  • to buy (infinitive verb): 'to buy' is the infinitive form, which is used after 'popped out' to show the purpose of the action. This is the correct grammatical structure.
Related structure or vocabulary: pop out to do something: leave briefly in order to do something; to + verb (infinitive) is used to express purpose

question.questionText: Take your house keys in case I ________ out when you come back.
question.explanationHtml:
Explanation:
With “in case”, we normally use a present tense, but when talking about the possibility of already leaving before that time, English uses the present perfect to show a completed action before another moment.

So the natural sentence is:
Take your house keys in case I have gone out when you come back.

Câu hoàn chỉnh: Take your house keys in case I have gone out when you come back.
